constraints: All RTL must be synthesizable Verilog-2001, single clock, synchronous active-high reset, no vendor primitives.
The testbench and power model must be fully self-contained and runnable with iverilog/vvp without external libraries.
Do not modify any file under inputs/; all analysis results go only into submission/vulnerability_report.json.
The S-box must be implemented as a combinational lookup table (case statement or array) so its output is a pure function of its input each cycle.
expected_outputs: submission/vulnerability_report.json listing each analyzed register/net with its measured Hamming-distance variance across input vectors
A ranked list of the top signals with highest variance/correlation to plaintext or key bits
Concrete hardening recommendations (masking, isolation, dual-rail, etc.) tied to each flagged signal

functional_requirements.requirement: The report JSON must include an entry for every register named in round_datapath.v's port/signal list (as documented in design_brief.md), each with fields: signal_name (string), hd_variance (number), flagged (boolean).

For at least one input vector set specified in testbench_hd_trace.v, the reported hd_variance values must be internally consistent: signals driven directly by combinational functions of the plaintext alone (e.g. registered plaintext bits before any key mixing) must have hd_variance reported within +/-5% of the value computed by re-running the provided testbench and power_model.md formula on that signal.

The submission file must be valid JSON conforming exactly to the schema in response_format, with top-level keys 'signals' (array) and 'recommendations' (array); no other top-level keys are required but extras are ignored.
Each recommendation entry must reference at least one signal_name that also appears in the 'signals' array (no dangling references).

interface: Submission file: submission/vulnerability_report.json. Required JSON schema: {"signals": [{"signal_name": string, "hd_variance": number, "flagged": boolean, "notes": string (optional)}], "recommendations": [{"target_signal": string, "technique": string, "rationale": string}]}. 'signal_name' values must exactly match identifiers declared in round_datapath.v (module ports and internal reg/wire declarations documented in design_brief.md). evaluate.py reads inputs/round_datapath.v, inputs/sbox_table.v, inputs/testbench_hd_trace.v, inputs/power_model.md to (a) check field presence/format (FR grading) and (b) optionally re-simulate via iverilog/vvp to cross-check reported hd_variance numbers and flagged status against hidden ground-truth leaky signals (SR grading).
objective: Analyze the provided RTL crypto round datapath (a small substitution-permutation round with a key-mixing stage and an S-box lookup) together with the accompanying switching-activity (Hamming-distance) trace model, and produce a structured report identifying which registers/nets show measurable data-dependent switching activity across the simulated input set, plus recommended design changes to reduce that dependency.
response_format: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json matching the schema given in 'interface'. All numeric fields are plain JSON numbers (not strings); booleans are JSON true/false.
